conversation.content:
Hello there — I’m so glad we have a chance to sit down together. My name is Claire, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician who works with new mothers as they settle into life after baby. To help me understand how you’ve been feeling lately, I’m going to use a short, well-trusted questionnaire called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**, or EPDS for short. It’s simply a 10-question check-in about the past seven days, and it helps us spot any signs of depression or anxiety that can sneak up during the postpartum year.  

Everything you share stays confidential between you, me, and whichever providers you choose to loop in, and there are no right or wrong answers — only what’s true for you. We’ll go through each question at your pace; if anything feels hard to talk about, we can pause or rephrase. When we’re finished, we’ll look at your score together and decide on next steps that feel manageable and supportive.  

Ready to start? Here’s the first question:  

Over the past seven days, how often have you been able to enjoy things — even little moments — that usually lift your mood?

Honestly… not very often. I still smile when the baby grasps my finger or when my toddler gives me one of those spontaneous hugs, but the little sparks fade fast. Even my favorite coffee or a short walk around the block feels kind of flat—like I can tell I “should” enjoy it, but the warmth just isn’t there the way it used to be.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I’ve laughed a few times—mostly when my older kid does something silly or when my husband makes a dumb joke—but it feels forced, like I have to remind myself to chuckle instead of it just bubbling up naturally.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. When I think about the weekend or a visit from my mom, I mostly feel tired before it even happens. I tell myself, “That should be nice,” but there’s no real spark of excitement—just another thing to get through.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Sometimes, yeah. Like yesterday the baby wouldn’t settle for his nap and I kept thinking I must be doing the routine wrong—maybe I rocked him too long or not enough. Rationally I know babies just have off days, but the thought still pops up that it’s my fault.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

A few times this week I’ve caught my heart racing while the baby’s napping, just staring at the monitor and worrying something might happen even though he’s breathing fine. There’s no real reason—I know he’s safe—but the anxious feeling shows up anyway.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Once or twice, mostly at night after I’ve finally laid the baby down. My chest gets tight and I feel kind of shaky, like something awful is about to happen, even though I can’t name what it is. It passes after a few minutes, but it’s unsettling.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah… some days it feels like the second I finish one thing—dishes, a feeding, a diaper change—there are three more waiting. I’m not falling apart, but I do end the evenings feeling like I’ve been barely treading water since breakfast.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

I wouldn’t say I’m “so unhappy,” but I do lie there with my mind racing—going over the next day’s feedings or worrying the baby might wake—and then I can’t drift off even when I’m exhausted. It’s happened three or four nights this week.
I have felt sad or miserable

I get waves of sadness, mostly in the late afternoon or when I’m alone with the baby and the house feels quiet. It’s not all day, but when it hits I feel kind of heavy and teary, and I have to force myself to keep moving through the routine.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
Not really—my eyes have watered a couple of times, but I haven’t actually cried. I mostly feel too tired to let it out, even when the sadness sits in my chest.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, never. I’ve felt overwhelmed and exhausted, but hurting myself hasn’t crossed my mind.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 18: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Summary

Patient: Postpartum mother, exact weeks post-delivery N/A  
Screener: Licensed MHP  
Date: [today]

** endorsed symptoms (self-report)  
- Anhedonia: markedly reduced ability to enjoy usual events; laughter described as “forced”  
- Low mood: daily waves of sadness, “heavy and teary,” most pronounced late afternoon/evening  
- Irrational guilt: self-blame when baby is fussy despite knowing “babies have off days”  
- Generalized & situational anxiety: racing heart while baby sleeps, anticipatory worry about next day tasks  
- Panic-type episodes: sudden chest tightness/shakiness at night, no identifiable trigger, resolves in minutes  
- Subjective overwhelm: feels “treading water,” tasks multiply faster than they are completed  
- Sleep-onset difficulty related to intrusive worries (3–4 nights/week)  
- No crying spells; no self-harm ideation 

Pattern: Symptoms interfere mainly with emotional coping and rest; patient remains functional in infant-care duties.  
Risk flags: Moderate—persistent low mood + anhedonia + anxiety without self-harm intent.  
Protective: denies suicidal/homicidal thoughts; reports partner and mother supports.

Screening impression: Meets criteria for further evaluation of **postpartum depression with co-occurring anxiety**; recommend formal assessment (PHQ-9, GAD-7, EPDS) and obstetric/primary care follow-up. Safety plan reviewed; immediate referral if suicidal ideation develops.
